title: AI-drafted variance commentary and management reporting packs, reviewed before release
problem: Variance explanations and performance narratives are written by hand, late in the reporting cycle; teams reported spending 47% of their time on data collection and validation.
approach: AI in planning platforms (Solver Copilot, Abacum) drafts variance summaries and proposes root causes; an analyst checks each against the ledger.
A named reviewer signs off before the pack goes to the client or board.
An unnamed media firm CFO said a flux agent built in three weeks cut commentary from 40 people to five reviewers (self-reported).
Finance teams reported spending an average of 26% of working time verifying or correcting AI-generated outputs (vendor-published).

title: Machine-generated baseline forecasts in planning software, with adviser judgment layered on top
problem: Client forecasting is a weeks-long process and hard to hold beyond a short horizon: 44% could plan with high confidence only up to three months ahead.
approach: Jirav Intelligent Forecasting uses AI and machine learning to build a cash-flow forecast from historical data; the advisor layers on client knowledge.
Analysts review and adjust machine baselines, and forecast error is tracked against actuals.
Creative Planning increased use from 10 clients to over 200, per Jirav's release (vendor-published).
64% of respondents in KPMG's survey of 1,013 senior finance leaders reported stronger forecast accuracy (self-reported).

title: Continuous driver-based planning with AI-assisted scenarios in place of the annual budget
problem: Planning horizons are shrinking and scenario work is slow: 44% can plan with high confidence only three months ahead, and 19% of teams can run a scenario within a day.
approach: Announced: RSM, Abacum, Grant Thornton and Gartner pitch rolling driver-based forecasts that update as the business changes, with what-if scenarios.
Abacum's release describes goal-seeking, such as reaching $125M without adding headcount.
Finance leaders set trigger thresholds and contingency actions; advisors challenge assumptions before scenarios go to management.
No outcome is published; the 19% scenario-speed figure is a baseline (vendor-published).

title: Automated budget input collection and approval routing in a planning platform
problem: Armanino's white paper describes budgets emailed as spreadsheets to dozens of people, with broken links, manual consolidation and no audit trail or role-based access.
approach: Abacum says its Workflow Intelligence layer automates budget input collection, approval routing and collaboration; consolidation changes are not described (vendor claim).
Approvers sign off submissions, and finance reviews the consolidated budget before release.
No outcome figures are published; Armanino pitches software-driven planning to replace the emailed-spreadsheet process.

title: Natural-language reporting, search and document-analysis agents in the planning platform
problem: At Cox Enterprises, per OneStream, finance had manual friction, hand-built ad hoc reports, answers buried in documentation and contracts reviewed line by line.
approach: Three agents: governed reports from plain-language requests, cited answers from approved finance documents, and structuring of large contract batches.
Users can inspect the sources and steps an agent used before relying on an answer.
Ad hoc report time fell from 10 minutes to one, and document lookup from eight minutes to 30 seconds (vendor-published).
Contract batch review time fell 67% to 98%, the presenter reports (vendor-published).

title: Governed planning data connected to general-purpose AI assistants
problem: Abacum says business users otherwise wait in the finance queue for answers, and that governed financial context is missing from the tools teams already use.
approach: Abacum says its workflow layer extends to Claude, ChatGPT and Slack through MCP connectors, giving users governed financial context.
Users validate answers against the governed model before using them in decisions.
Xero integrated Anthropic's Claude on May 12, 2026, per Accountex coverage; Karbon scheduled a session on building automations with Claude Code.

title: Planning models built and changed in plain language by agents
problem: Building and changing multidimensional planning models normally needs specialist administrators or implementation consultants.
approach: Abacum says Modeling Intelligence lets finance teams build and modify models in plain language, with agents adding entities, currencies and product lines.
Abacum says agents cascade updates without breaking downstream reports; RSM's page says models build quickly without specialist admins while keeping auditability.
A reviewer inspects structural changes and reconciles outputs to the prior model before release.
No outcome figures are published (vendor claim).

title: AI-assisted opportunity analysis for pricing, cost and driver diagnosis
problem: Gartner says the best AI opportunities are material problems that are hard to diagnose with traditional methods, while many initiatives still aim at incremental improvements.
approach: Language models and analytics find and size improvement opportunities; business and finance leaders validate them before commitments.
In KPMG's article, an unnamed automotive company used AI and language models to scrape pricing data and optimise its parts business.
That use saved $100 million 'this year alone', according to KPMG's article (self-reported).
EXL's profile in ISG's report cites cost command centers and contract intelligence for CFO decision support.

title: AI readiness and data-foundation assessment with a prioritised use-case roadmap
problem: Mid-market clients use AI widely but have not made it work at scale, and the barriers named most often are data quality and integration rather than the models.
approach: Advisers run a diagnostic first: surveys, interviews, maturity assessment, benchmarking and phased roadmap (CFGI's five-week Phase 0), plus data-readiness checks (CohnReznick).
Executive sessions agree vision and priorities; findings are reviewed with finance leadership before any build.
Citrin Cooperman acquired AI consulting firm Rosetree Solutions, effective 2026-10-01, to give middle-market clients AI implementation.
No firm-side outcome is published; 53% of organisations with limited pilot success named data quality as a barrier, 47% integration (self-reported).
who: CFGI, CohnReznick, Cherry Bekaert, Citrin Cooperman

title: Advisory firms pair AI-embedded planning platforms with finance planning services
problem: Planning, budgeting and forecasting still run on spreadsheets and legacy tools; Armanino describes budgets emailed to dozens of people and consolidated by hand, with no audit trail.
approach: Announced: firms pair AI-enabled planning platforms with their own implementation practice, such as RSM with Abacum and CFGI with Abacum.
Armanino lists Abacum and Solver, CohnReznick Workday Adaptive Planning, and Forvis Mazars Solver on Business Central.
Advisors design and validate the model structure; users are trained to interpret AI insights and apply professional judgment (CohnReznick).
CohnReznick's page says to accelerate planning and reporting cycle times by 50-70% (vendor-published).
who: RSM, CFGI, Armanino, CohnReznick, Forvis Mazars

title: Advisory partners enable and govern AI agents built into mid-market ERP software
problem: ERP vendors ship AI assistants and agents with each release, and clients need someone to decide which to turn on, set roles and permissions, and connect workflows.
approach: Announced: Armanino's August 12, 2026 deck says Sage Intacct's Finance Intelligence Agent is rolling out to all customers 'this summer and fall'.
Partner firms run release webinars and offer agent services; Rand Group says it helps enable native agents in Microsoft, NetSuite and Sage.
An administrator enables each agent and sets role access; marketplace agents are certified by the vendor.
No outcome is published for the advisory service (vendor-published).
who: Armanino, EisnerAmper, Rand Group, Sage Intacct

title: Partner-delivered implementation of AI-native ERP for mid-market finance teams
problem: Rillet says legacy ERPs act as 'dumb databases' where the real work happens in spreadsheets, and that traditional implementations take about 12 months.
approach: Announced: Rillet's AI-native ERP applies AI inside the general ledger; Rillet names Armanino and Wiss as accounting-firm partners.
The implementation partner designs the chart of accounts, integrations and controls.
Rillet says customers report implementing in as little as 4 weeks versus 12 months, and closing in a few days (vendor-published).

title: Managed finance planning with agent-led forecasting and variance analysis, priced on outcomes
problem: Enterprises want external help with planning, forecasting and decision support, not only transactional finance, and are comfortable sourcing more of it.
approach: ISG's September 2026 quadrant says providers apply predictive models and GenAI to variance analysis, scenarios and forecasts, with early agentic capability.
ISG describes PwC's outcomes-based managed service with agent-led forecasting, plus offerings from EY, Deloitte, EXL and Sutherland.
ISG describes EY's framework as turning variance analysis that took thousands of hours into minutes (vendor-published).
Agentic capabilities operate under human oversight; sign-off points are not specified.
who: ISG, PwC, EY, Deloitte, EXL, Sutherland

title: Idea: validation and sign-off service for AI-generated forecasts and commentary
problem: Idea, not a deployment: finance leaders hesitate to trust AI for critical work; in a vendor survey 75% cited lack of auditability and 71% accuracy concerns.
approach: Idea only: practitioners describe an agent inventory with named owners, replayable evidence, risk-scaled sign-off gates and a kill threshold for errors.
A short pilot would measure time saved, review time and errors; humans approve outputs before financial statements or board reporting.
COSO's February 2026 guidance maps generative AI capabilities to its 17 control principles; Grant Thornton's August 2026 webcast covers forecasting governance.
